hypothesis: The current Digital Twin W0-W4 applies different hidden outcome mechanisms to exactly matched PRE support, so prediction-time PRE cannot identify the world label and W0-W4 cannot fairly evaluate a learned PRE-only regime selector.
input_dataset: Source-independent Digital Twin only; seed 20260916; 500 matched standard 7-rider synthetic race identities evaluated under W0-W4; 2500 world-labeled synthetic samples total; no real/historical race input.
prediction_method: No predictive model was trained. For each matched synthetic race, canonical PRE hashes were compared across W0-W4 and hidden oracle distributions were compared by total-variation distance. Empirical H(world), H(world|PRE), and I(PRE;world) were computed from the matched support.
conclusion: PASS_CURRENT_W0_W4_PRE_NONIDENTIFIABILITY_CONFIRMED. Across all 500 matched race identities, PRE was byte-equivalent by canonical hash under every W0-W4 label, every PRE group contained each of the five world labels exactly once, and empirical I(PRE;world) was numerically zero. At the same time, hidden oracle distributions were materially different: mean pairwise total-variation distance was 0.1391 and the minimum pair mean was 0.0516. Therefore the current W0-W4 twin can test universal robustness but cannot fairly test a learned PRE-only regime selector, because the stress-regime identity is absent from PRE by construction.
scientific_implication: Do not respond to V1/V2 failures by tuning an adaptive W0-W4 selector: that problem is unidentifiable from PRE. Preserve W0-W4 as universal robustness stress lanes. If regime adaptation is to be studied, create a separately versioned Digital Twin in which the outcome mechanism varies as a preregistered deterministic function of PRE-observable variables while outcomes remain hidden and no direct world label is exposed.
follow_up: Preserve W0-W4 unchanged. Build a separately versioned learnable-regime synthetic twin whose hidden mechanism intensity is a fixed deterministic function of PRE-observable variables, then preregister a development/evaluation comparison between universal and PRE-adaptive probability objects using disjoint synthetic seeds. No real data, economics, or promotion claim.
